s1loc: Chapeltown sits in north Sheffield, where food aid leans on the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks. FareShare Yorkshire moves surplus to community groups across the region, while Trussell-network foodbanks such as Sheffield S6 hand out emergency parcels nearby. St Luke's Hospice, Sheffield's hospice, runs charity shops on Lound Side and Station Road in Chapeltown, funding care from local donations. High Green Development Trust coordinates cost-of-living vouchers across High Green, Chapeltown, Burncross, Grenoside and Ecclesfield for households on prepayment meters.

The sector runs at every size. Regional names like St Luke's keep charity shops and central buying across Sheffield, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Burncross, Grenoside, Ecclesfield and High Green. The Chapeltown and Burncross Community Centre on Burncross Road and the Grenoside Community Centre host volunteer-led groups and food support sessions in church and community halls. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Beyond the foodbanks, the local effort runs through Voluntary Action Sheffield and grants from the South Yorkshire's Community Foundation, which channel money to grass-roots outfits. Ecclesfield Parish Council lists dozens of local groups, from the Royal British Legion in Chapeltown to friends-of-park volunteers improving Chapeltown park. Charity shops cluster on Station Road and through Ecclesfield, and mutual-aid crews and pantry teams cover Burncross, Thorncliffe and High Green, all run by volunteers who need hard-wearing branded kit for sorting, shop floors and collection days.

s1loc: Stalybridge sits in eastern Tameside, where Tameside East Foodbank runs the Trussell-network effort from Holy Trinity and Christ Church on Corporation Street, with centres across Ashton-under-Lyne, Dukinfield, Millbrook and Stalybridge. More than 105 local agencies issue vouchers to people in crisis. FareShare moves surplus food to community groups across Greater Manchester, and Tameside Council lists community pantries alongside the foodbanks. Holy Trinity Stalybridge hosts a long-running food bank session staffed by church volunteers.

The sector runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying along Melbourne Street and Market Street, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Millbrook, Dukinfield, Carrbrook and Heyrod. The Tameside East Foodbank collects from churches, schools and businesses and sorts donations entirely with volunteers across its four centres. We supply the national charity with shops town-wide and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum order.

Beyond the foodbank, Stalybridge's voluntary scene runs through Action Together, the support body for Tameside's charities and volunteers, which matches local people to grass-roots roles. Charity shops line the town centre and Market Street, raising funds for national and regional causes, and community groups gather at venues like Stalybridge Civic Hall. Mutual-aid teams and warm-space sessions cover Millbrook, Heyrod and Carrbrook, all run by volunteers who need durable branded kit for sorting bays, shop counters and community collection days.

s1loc: Workington sits on the west Cumbrian coast, where North Lakes Foodbank runs the Trussell-network effort, with a centre at The Bridge Centre on Central Square open three days a week and further sites in Cockermouth, Maryport, Whitehaven, Wigton and Egremont. FareShare Lancashire and Cumbria, operated by Recycling Lives, redistributes surplus food to grass-roots groups across the region. Cumbria Community Foundation channels grants to local projects, and a community food pantry runs on Trinity Drive at Northside.

The sector runs at every size. Hospice at Home West Cumbria keeps charity shops on Pow Street in Workington and in Cockermouth, with a donation centre and around 86 retail volunteers, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Moorclose, Northside, Salterbeck and Harrington. Moorclose Community Centre runs regular community food pantries. We serve the national charity with shops town-wide and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum order.

Beyond the foodbanks, the wider effort runs through Cumbria CVS, which lists volunteering across Allerdale and matches local people to roles, and the Cumbria Community Foundation responds to need with grants to small charities. Charity shops cluster along Pow Street and the town centre, raising funds for the hospice and national causes, and mutual-aid and warm-space teams cover Moorclose, Northside and Harrington. All are run by volunteers who need hard-wearing branded kit for sorting, shop floors and coastal collection days.

s1loc: Walton-on-Thames sits in the borough of Elmbridge, where Walton Charity runs the Walton and Hersham Foodbank with more than 60 volunteers, helping over 100 people a week from sessions in three churches plus The Bridge, its family support hub at 17 Bridge Street in the town centre. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks supply community groups across Surrey, and Walton Charity also runs a community allotment on Terrace Road for people to meet and learn new skills.

The sector runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying along the High Street and Hersham, while Princess Alice Hospice in nearby Esher runs a retail hub at Hersham Green feeding more than 40 shops. Small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Hersham, Halfway, Ashley Park and Oatlands. We serve the national charity with shops town-wide and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum order.

Beyond the foodbank, the local effort runs through the Elmbridge Volunteer Centre and Central Surrey Voluntary Action, which match volunteers to charitable roles across the borough. Walton Charity itself is a long-standing charitable foundation tackling poverty, health, housing and education across Elmbridge. Charity shops cluster along the High Street, and mutual-aid teams, warm spaces and pantry crews cover Hersham, Halfway and Oatlands, all run by volunteers who need durable branded kit for sorting bays, shop counters and community events.

s1loc: Esher sits in the borough of Elmbridge, home to Princess Alice Hospice on West End Lane, a Surrey charity that relies on more than 1,200 volunteers and runs charity shops and a retail hub at Hersham Green supplying over 40 stores. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks supply community groups across the borough, and the nearby Walton and Hersham Foodbank, run by Walton Charity, hands out emergency parcels to households in crisis from sessions across Elmbridge.

The sector runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying through Esher High Street, Claygate and Hersham, with Princess Alice Hospice shops at The Parade in Claygate and the Hersham Centre. Small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Claygate, Hersham, Thames Ditton and Hinchley Wood. We serve the national charity with shops town-wide and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum order.

Beyond the hospice, the local effort runs through Central Surrey Voluntary Action, the volunteer centre covering Elmbridge, Epsom and Ewell and Mole Valley, which matches volunteers to charitable roles. Princess Alice runs a Compassionate Neighbours scheme placing trained volunteers alongside people in the community. Claygate sustains a busy roster of community organisations and groups, and charity shops cluster through Claygate Parade and Thames Ditton, all run by volunteers who need hard-wearing branded kit for shop floors, sorting and community fundraising days.

s1loc: Whitefield sits in the borough of Bury, where Trust House on Bury Old Road runs a community centre and food pantry, opened in 2019 to tackle food poverty, fuel insecurity and mental health, with a low-cost weekly pantry of fresh and tinned food. FareShare Greater Manchester redistributes surplus to community groups across the region, and Trinity Food Bank, a member of the Bury Community Support Network, distributes from the GTR centre in nearby Radcliffe. Trust House covers Whitefield, Prestwich and Crumpsall.

The sector runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying along Bury New Road and Whitefield centre, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Besses o' th' Barn, Unsworth, Park Lane and Prestwich. Porch Boxes, a volunteer-run Bury charity, packs around 450 crisis food packs a month from its Bradley Fold warehouse for local agencies. We serve the national charity with shops town-wide and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum order.

Beyond the pantry, the wider effort runs through Bury VCFA, the borough's voluntary-sector support body, which funds and develops local charities and matches volunteers to roles, and helped fund Trust House's community cafe, warm space and food pantry. Charity shops cluster through Whitefield centre and Bury New Road, and community groups, mutual-aid crews and warm spaces cover Besses o' th' Barn, Unsworth and Park Lane, all run by volunteers who need durable branded kit for pantry sorting, shop counters and community events.

s1loc: Potters Bar sits in the borough of Hertsmere, where Potters Bar Foodbank, part of the Trussell network and registered as Blaze 4:16, runs from the Jubilee Wayside Community Centre on Wayside, working with over 20 local agencies including Hertsmere Council and Citizens Advice to issue vouchers. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks supply community groups across the area, and the foodbank is part of Hertsmere's Food Poverty Alliance, a partnership tackling food poverty across the borough.

The sector runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying through Darkes Lane and the High Street, with a Cancer Research UK shop in town, while small foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Little Heath, Cranborne and Bentley Heath. Rennie Grove Peace Hospice Care runs a support hub at the Wyllyotts Centre for people with life-limiting illness. We serve the national charity with shops town-wide and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum order.

Beyond the foodbank, the local effort draws on Hertsmere's Food Poverty Alliance partners and the volunteer-run sessions that weigh, sort and store donated food before parcels go out. The Wyllyotts Centre anchors community activity, hosting wellbeing sessions and drop-ins, and charity shops cluster along Darkes Lane. Mutual-aid teams and warm spaces cover Little Heath, Cranborne and Bentley Heath, all run by volunteers who need hard-wearing branded kit for sorting bays, shop counters and community collection days.
